title: Trump Announces 'Energy Ceasefire' Between Russia and Ukraine
summary:
On Sunday, U.S. President Donald Trump said Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire." A ceasefire is an agreement to stop attacking. This one would mean the two countries stop striking each other's power plants and other energy sites. Russia and Ukraine have been at war for about four and a half years.

Trump's short social media post said the ceasefire began right away, and added, "Do not break it!" He did not give any other details. Russia did not immediately comment.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine "welcomed" the announcement as "good news for everyone." But he said Russia was still attacking energy sites in Kyiv, Ukraine's capital, and in the city of Kharkiv, using drones and bombs. He said a power plant in Kharkiv was attacked that evening.

Zelenskyy said Ukraine was "ready to refrain from striking Russian energy infrastructure" if Russia did the same. Earlier on Sunday, he asked Trump to press Russia to stop hitting Ukraine's energy system. Ukrainian officials say Russia has tried to cut off power, heat and water to wear down people during the war.

This is not the first such announcement. On September 14, Trump said both countries had agreed not to hit each other's energy sites, but nothing came of that plan.

The two leaders have also disagreed in public. On Saturday, Trump said it was time for Ukraine to get a new president. Zelenskyy answered that choosing a leader is up to Ukraine's people. Ukraine's constitution does not allow elections while the country is under martial law, which is special wartime rule.

On Friday, Trump also made a deal to buy diesel fuel from Russia to try to lower high U.S. fuel prices. Ukrainian and European officials criticized that deal.
why_it_matters: Attacks on power plants can leave families without electricity, heat and water, so a real energy ceasefire could protect civilians. Whether this announcement holds will show how much U.S. diplomacy can change the war.

background_read: Russia launched a full invasion of its neighbor Ukraine, and the two countries have been fighting ever since.
Both sides have attacked energy sites such as power plants, which can leave people without electricity, heat or water.
A ceasefire is a promise to stop certain attacks, but it only works if both sides follow it.
The United States has tried to help the two countries reach deals that could reduce the fighting.
